summary: This note traces the names used for Myanmar, focusing on the country's official English name changes and the earliest known written use of the name 'Mranma'. It notes that the 1989 renaming and later official name have been controversial and inconsistently adopted. It also describes the Yadana Kon Htan Inscription, a stone from the Bagan period that contains the earliest recorded use of the name.
one_line: Overview of Myanmar's official English name changes since 1989 and the earliest recorded use of 'Mranma' on the Yadana Kon Htan Inscription.
key_facts: In 1989 the government changed the official English name from the Union of Burma to the Union of Myanmar.
The official English name was later changed to the Republic of the Union of Myanmar.
The name changes have been the subject of controversies and mixed incidences of adoption.
Ma Thanegi records that the first use of the name 'Mranma' for the country is found on a stone inscription.
The stone inscription is 3 feet (91 cm) high.
The stone inscription is dated 597 ME (Traditional Burmese calendar) or 1235 CE.
The stone is from the reign of Kyaswa (1234 - 1250), son of King Htilominlo (Nadaungmya), Bagan.
The stone is written in early Burmese script.
The middle of the front side of the stone is damaged.
The first line of the better-protected reverse side shows မြန်မာပြည် ('Mranma kingdom').
The inscription is known as the 'Yadana Kon Htan Inscription'.
The inscription is held at Bagan and recorded as stone number 43 in the Archaeological Department's collection.
